rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The verse was revealed after Thabit ibn Rifaʿa’s father died and his uncle asked the Prophet when he could use and return the orphan’s property.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة

rows.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد
rows.claim: They interpret testing orphans as assessing their intellect and religious conduct.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد: اختبروهم في عقولهم وأديانهم

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Guardians test a near-pubescent boy by entrusting a little spending money; a girl is tested through household management and spinning cotton.
rows.anchor: يرد إليه الأمر في نفقته عند مراهقة الحلم، ويعطى شيئا نزرا يتصرف فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد
rows.claim: They understand reaching marriage age as attaining puberty, specifically a wet dream.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد: يريد الحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means reaching the condition for marriage through seminal emission.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا بلغوا حال النكاح من الاحتلام

rows.speaker: آخرون؛ ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Another interpretation is reaching adult capacity for marriage; Ibn Qutayba says becoming able to marry women.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: أي بلغوا مبلغ الرجال والنساء من القدرة على النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A boy or girl reaches maturity upon ejaculation, whether through intercourse or a wet dream.
rows.anchor: فإذا أنزل الغلام أو الجارية فقد بلغ، سواء كان عن جماع أو احتلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ عطاء عنه؛ الفراء؛ الزجاج
rows.claim: The glosses for anastum are knowing, seeing, finding, and knowing, respectively.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وجدتم (¬3). وقال الزجاج: علمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of īnās is seeing; the cited verse and Ibn Ḥalaza’s line use it for perceiving or finding something.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإيناس في اللغة: الإبصار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Guardians must not hasten to consume orphans’ property extravagantly before they reach puberty and sound judgment.
rows.anchor: يريد لا تبادروا في أموال اليتامى بالسرف قبل أن يبلغ الحلم والرشد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Guardians may rush to consume the estate out of fear that maturity will require them to hand it over.
rows.anchor: لا تبادروا بأكل مالهم كبرهم ورشدهم حذرا أن يبلغوا فيلزمكم تسليم المال إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is accusative as the object of the verbal noun, meaning hastening their maturity.
rows.anchor: و (أن) في محل النصب؛ لأنه مفعول المصدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian must refrain entirely from the orphan’s property.
rows.anchor: من كان غنيا من الأوصياء فليستعفف عن مال اليتيم ولا يأكل منه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiʿfāf means leaving the property and not eating from it.
rows.anchor: أي: ليترك ذلك ولا يأكل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، وعبيدة، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، وأكثر الروايات عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A poor guardian may borrow only what he needs, repay upon becoming able, and owes nothing if he dies unable; verse 4:114 supports construing maʿrūf as a loan, as does ʿUmar’s practice.
rows.anchor: هو أن يأخذ بقدر ما يحتاج إليه من

rows.speaker: عطاء، وعكرمة، والسدي
rows.claim: A poor guardian may take a moderate amount without extravagance and need not repay it.
rows.anchor: معنى الأكل بالمعروف هو أن يقتصد ولا يسرف، ثم لا قضاء عليه فيما يأكل

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: A guardian may take only enough to relieve hunger and cover nakedness.
rows.anchor: هو ما سد الجوعة ووارى العورة

rows.speaker: عائشة وجماعة من العلماء
rows.claim: A guardian may take a fair wage proportionate to work, even from the whole estate, without repayment; a report from Ibn ʿAbbās permits eating without hoarding or protecting one’s own wealth with the orphan’s.
rows.anchor: أن يأخذ من جميع المال إذا كان يلي ذلك بقدر قيامه وعمله وأجرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian may not be extravagant and is entitled only to the market-rate wage for his legally assigned work; the wealthy must abstain.
rows.anchor: القيم ممنوع من الإسراف، وإنما له أجر مثل عمله؛ لأنه أجير بالشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing the transfer protects the guardian with evidence if a dispute arises; it is recommended, not obligatory, and the orphan’s word prevails because the guardian is a trustee.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن القول قول اليتيم عند التنازع

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري والأزهري
rows.claim: Ḥasīban can mean an accountant or one who suffices.
rows.anchor: يكون بمعنى محاسبا، ويكون بمعنى كافيا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: In a threat, ḥasībuhu Allāh means God will hold him accountable; Qays al-Majnūn’s poem uses ḥasīb in that sense.
rows.anchor: فمعناه: ثم أنت محاسبها على ظلمها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī’s verse likewise uses ḥasīb for the one who will account for a wrong.
rows.anchor: فلا تدخلن الدهر قبرك حوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ḥasīb means sufficient, ḥasībuka Allāh means God is enough for you; compare the phrase in Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: ومن الكفاية قولهم: حسيبك الله. ومعناه: كافي إياك الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God is the requiter of both the good and the evildoer, returning to the sense of accounting.
rows.anchor: يريد مجازيا للحسن والمسيء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The prefixed bāʾ in “God is sufficient” constructions is extra, so the meaning is simply that God or the Lord suffices.
rows.anchor: المعنى: كفى الله، كفى ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasīban is accusative either as a circumstantial qualifier or as specification distinguishing God from those who suffice or account.
rows.anchor: وحسيبا منصوب على وجهين: أحدهما الحال

rows.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
rows.claim: They are losers because they traded faith for disbelief, destroying their own souls in punishment; the gravest work-loss is a ruined soul, as commerce’s worst loss is its capital.
rows.anchor: باعوا الإيمان بالكفر، فعظم خسرانهم في ذلك البيع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Meeting God means resurrection, reward, punishment, and return to Him; the author links this explanation to 2:46.
rows.anchor: يريد بالبعث والثواب والعقاب والمصير إليه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The phrase means meeting God’s recompense; “meeting God” names meeting one’s deeds’ recompense, as people say a dead person met his deeds.
rows.anchor: المعنى هاهنا كذبوا # بلقاء جزاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā marks the endpoint of their denial: they denied until the Resurrection appeared suddenly and regret began.
rows.anchor: {حتى} هاهنا بيان أن منتهى تكذيبهم الحسرة يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The Hour is the Day of Resurrection, so called because reckoning and recompense are completed with extraordinary speed.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة الساعة؛ لسرعة الحساب للجزاء فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is the time when Resurrection begins, named for its sudden onset; this better fits baghtatan, which means suddenly.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أصح. ألا ترى أنه قال: {بغتة} والبغت والبغتة (¬3): الفجأة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: No one knows when the Hour will come except God, so it catches people unawares.
rows.anchor: يريد أن الساعة لا يعلمها أحد إلا هو

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Calling out “our regret” alerts hearers to a terrible calamity and is more emphatic than simply saying regret is upon us; Arabic figurative address can target someone other than the literal addressee.
rows.anchor: معنى دعاء الحسرة: تنبيه الناس على ما وقع بهم من الحسرة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The vocative summons regret as if telling it to come: this is your time; thus “our regret” means attend to our loss.
rows.anchor: تأويل يا حسرتاه: انتبهوا على أنا قد خسرنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد، وأبو عبيدة، وأكثر أهل اللغة، والحسن
rows.claim: Farraṭnā means we neglected or wasted; the regret concerns abandoned work for the Afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي: تركنا وضيعنا فيها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Farraṭnā means we put incapacity first, construing neglect as bringing shortcoming forward.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: {فرطنا}: قدمنا العجز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The pronoun in fīhā refers to worldly life.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (في الدنيا)

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Hour: they neglected the work and preparation needed for it.
rows.anchor: روي عن الحسن أنه قال: (في الساعة)

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Paradise, meaning they neglected seeking it and working for it.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي (في الجنة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the implied deeds themselves: regret over good works and acts of obedience that they neglected.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تعود الكناية إلى معنى {ما}

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the implied transaction: the preceding mention of loss signals the sale.
rows.anchor: الكناية تعود إلى الصفقة؛ لأنه لما ذكر الخسران دل على الصفقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
rows.claim: Awzār are the heavy burden of sin: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses them as sins and errors, while al-Zajjāj says they carry the weight of their sins.
rows.anchor: يريد آثامهم وخطاياهم

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Wizr originally means a load one carries, explaining both sins as burdens and the phrase “no bearer bears”; the root also appears in ordinary loading and in “minister.”
rows.anchor: الوزر الثقل، وأصله من الحمل

rows.speaker: المفسرون؛ قتادة؛ السدي
rows.claim: Good and evil deeds appear as riders after resurrection: the believer rides beautiful, fragrant good work, while the unbeliever is ridden by foul, ugly evil work; this explains the image of bearing sins.
rows.anchor: إن المؤمن إذا خرج من قبره استقبله أحسن شيء سورة وأطيبه ريحا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Bearing sins can figuratively describe enduring punishment as a crushing weight, since heaviness describes emotional states as well as physical loads.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل جائز أن يكون جعل ما ينالهم من العذاب بمنزلة أثقل

rows.speaker: أهل العربية
rows.claim: The image may mean sins never leave them, like saying someone’s person is before one’s eyes to mean the person remains constantly in mind.
rows.anchor: لا تزايلهم أوزارهم، كما تقول: شخصك نصب عيني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the load as an evil burden; al-Zajjāj says what they carry is a bad thing, with the wording discussed at 4:22.
rows.anchor: يريد بئس الحمل حملوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abraham’s people disputed with and argued against him about their gods, using them to frighten him.
rows.anchor: خاصمه وجادله في آلهتهم وخوفوه بها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Their debate concerned stars, sun, moon, and idols; Abraham’s question rejects argument against God’s oneness after God had shown him guidance.
rows.anchor: فيما عبدوا مع الله جل وعز من الكواكب والشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke denying that they can argue him away from the guidance he has received.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستفهام معناه الإنكار للمحاجة في الصرف عن الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The geminated nūn in tuḥājjūnnī joins two nūns by assimilation; Nāfiʿ reads a light nūn after deleting one, with the second deleted because it is heavier and the first marks inflection.
rows.anchor: نافع مخففة النون حذف إحدى النونين تخفيفا

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: A line attributed to ʿAmr illustrates deleting the second nūn that accompanies the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قول عمرو: تراه كالثغام يعل مسكا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: They warned Abraham that their gods could afflict him with madness, explaining his denial that he feared them.
rows.anchor: خوفوه آلهتهم أن يصيبه منها خبل

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The worshipped objects neither harm nor benefit; the exception means “but I fear my Lord’s will to punish me,” with an accusative clause and a disconnected exception.
rows.anchor: لا تضر (¬3) ولا تنفع ولا أخافها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The will, illnesses, and diseases are under God’s control, answering their warning that the idols might harm Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬7): (يريد: أن المشيئة والأسقام والأمراض إليه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How should I fear?” is a rhetorical denial and a challenge to prove that Abraham’s fear is justified.
rows.anchor: معناه: الإنكار للخوف، وهو سؤال تعجيز عن تصحيح الخوف بالبرهان

rows.speaker: author؛ ابن عباس
rows.claim: The objects associated with God are idols, and “without authority” means without any proof; sulṭān is power or evidence that enables one to prevail.
rows.anchor: والسلطان قوة وحجة يتمكن بها ويتسلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks which deserves security from punishment, the monotheist or the idolater.
rows.anchor: أي: أحق بأن يأمن العذاب الموحد أم المشرك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The words about those who believe and do not mix faith with wrongdoing continue Abraham’s argument, as if a learned speaker asks and answers himself.
rows.anchor: هذا من قول إبراهيم لقومه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The words are Abraham’s people replying to his question about which group deserves security, using the verse as their answer.
rows.anchor: قوم إبراهيم لإبراهيم أجابوه لما سألهم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The words are God’s own verdict distinguishing Abraham and his adherents from the other group.
rows.anchor: هذا من قول الله تعالى على جهة فصل القضاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ سعيد بن جبير؛ ابن جريج
rows.claim: Wrongdoing here means associating partners with God, or disbelief and shirk; Ibn Jurayj says no one disputed that interpretation.
rows.anchor: لم يخلطوا إيمانهم بشرك

rows.speaker: علقمة عن ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When Muslims feared that any personal sin invalidated security, the Prophet explained that the verse means shirk and cited Luqmān’s description of shirk as grave wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ألم تسمعوا ما قال لقمان لابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves that whoever dies without associating partners with God must ultimately be secure from the Fire.
rows.anchor: من مات لا يشرك بالله وجب أن يكون عاقبته الأمن من النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The promised security is from punishment, and the guided are directed to God’s religion.
rows.anchor: يريد: من العذاب، {وهم مهتدون} يريد: أرشدوا إلى دين الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Mā is accusative as the object of atlu: recite what your Lord has forbidden.
rows.anchor: موضع (ما) نصب ب (أتل)، أي: اتل الذي حرمه ربكم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: An lā tushrikū can be accusative after an omitted lām, explaining what is forbidden; inventing religious prohibitions makes their inventors partners with God in authority.
rows.anchor: لأنهم إذا حرموا ما أحل الله عز وجل فقد جعلوا غير الله في القبول منه بمنزلة الله

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is construed by meaning as “I recite to you the prohibition of shirk” or “I enjoin you not to associate,” parallel to the command to show kindness to parents.
rows.anchor: قال: ويجوز أن يكون {ألا تشركوا به}

rows.speaker: أبو بكر؛ الفراء
rows.claim: Another analysis makes an accusative after ʿalaykum as exhortation, or nominative like “upon you is fasting”; al-Farrāʾ allows tushrikū to be subjunctive after an or jussive after lā, preferring jussive for the following commands, which may mix moods.
rows.anchor: والجزم في هذه الآية أحب إلي لقوله: {وأوفوا الكيل والميزان}

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: The command to show kindness to parents has an understood verb: “and that you do kindness,” coordinated with “that you not associate.”
rows.anchor: التقدير: أن لا تشركوا به شيئا وأن تفعلوا {وبالوالدين إحسانا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
rows.claim: Killing children from imlāq means fear of poverty; the parallel wording in 17:31 explicitly says fear of poverty and refers to burying daughters alive, from jealousy or want, while promising provision.
rows.anchor: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Amlaq can be intransitive for becoming poor and transitive for destroying what one owns; imlāq can mean ruin.
rows.anchor: أملق الرجل فهو مملق إذا افتقر

rows.speaker: ابن شميل؛ أوس بن حجر
rows.claim: A line by Aws ibn Ḥajar uses amlaqa for calamities consuming a person’s property.
rows.anchor: وأملق ما عندي خطوب تنبل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: People who avoided public adultery still committed it secretly; the prohibition covers both hidden and open fornication.
rows.anchor: كانوا يكرهون أن يزنوا علانية فيفعلون ذلك سرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Killing a protected soul “except by right” means legal retaliation, qiṣāṣ.
rows.anchor: إلا بالقود يريد: القصاص

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The phrase “that is what He enjoins” shows that the preceding commands mean “He enjoins you not to associate partners and to show kindness to parents.”
rows.anchor: هذا يدل على أن معنى {ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا} محمول

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A needy guardian who improves and tends the orphan’s property may take a customary amount; a wealthy one abstains, in line with 2:220’s emphasis on improving orphans’ welfare.
rows.anchor: إن كنت له وصيا فأصلحت في ماله وقمت لله في ضيعته

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The guardian should seek growth for the orphan through investment and take none of its profit.
rows.anchor: هو أن يبتغي له فيه من فضل الله ولا يأخذ من ربحه شيئا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The best management of the orphan’s property is to trade with it.
rows.anchor: هو التجارة فيه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق؛ السدي
rows.claim: The best management is to preserve and grow the orphan’s assets as far as possible.
rows.anchor: حفظ ماله عليه وتثميره بما يوجد السبيل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Until the orphan comes of age means preserve the estate until maturity, then hand it over.
rows.anchor: حتى محمولة على المعنى أي: احفظوه عليه حتى يبلغ أشده

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Ashudd is the point at which a man reaches mature judgment and knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: (الأشد: مبلغ الرجل الحنكة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد عن الفراء
rows.claim: Farrāʾ says ashudd would theoretically have singular shadd, though he had not heard one; a poem supplies an example of the plural.
rows.anchor: الأشد واحدها شد في القياس، ولم أسمع لها بواحد

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: The singular is shidda, strength and toughness; the feminine ending is treated as extra when forming the plural on afʿul, like rajul/arjul.
rows.anchor: واحدة الأشد: شدة، كما أن واحدة الأنعم: نعمة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري؛ جماعة من البصريين
rows.claim: Some linguists treat ashudd as a singular without a singular form; some Basrans give its singular as shudd with a ḍamma.
rows.anchor: أن واحده: شد بضم الشين

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: The span of ashudd begins at adult maturity and ends at forty, with the endpoints fixed but the interval unspecified; 46:15 also links ashudd and forty.
rows.anchor: وبلوغ الأشد يكون من وقت بلوغ الإنسان مبلغ الرجال وإدراكه إلى أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر؛ السدي
rows.claim: In this verse, reaching ashudd is interpreted as puberty, specifically a wet dream.
rows.anchor: وفسر بلوغ الأشد في هذه الآية بالاحتلام

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The orphan must be both physically mature and sound in judgment before receiving his money; the author refers back to the discussion at the start of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبلوغ أشده أن يونس منه الرشد مع أن يكون بالغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafāʾ means completion; fulfilling the measure means giving its full amount without short measure.
rows.anchor: وأوفى الكيل، أي: أتمه ولم ينقص منه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mīzān means weighing with the scale, not completing the scale itself; the wording omits the understood noun “weight,” just as “measure” omits “measuring vessel.”
rows.anchor: أي: وزن الميزان والوزن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisṭ means justice, with neither shortchanging nor excess.
rows.anchor: بالعدل لا بخس ولا شطط

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: God has made lawful and unlawful dealings known; sellers should give buyers the full measure they themselves want when purchasing.
rows.anchor: فكما تحب أن يوفيك من تشتري منه، فأوف من تبيع منه

rows.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
rows.claim: The seller must give the exact due without extra burden, and the buyer must accept the exact due without demanding a shortfall; neither is required to do what exceeds capacity.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه الذي هو له من غير زيادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
rows.claim: When speaking or testifying, tell the truth even if the person concerned is a child, relative, or someone beloved; the omitted party may be either witness beneficiary or accused, as al-Zajjāj explains, paralleling 5:106.
rows.anchor: إذا شهدتم أو تكلمتم فقولوا الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant with God’s name is explained by the discussion of keeping covenants at 2:40.
rows.anchor: العهد عند قوله: {وأوفوا بعهدي}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing command gathers orphan-property care, just measures, capacity, truth even about relatives, and keeping promises, so people remember and act on them; the promise reward is cited at 48:10.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي تقدم من ذكر مال اليتيم، وأن لا يقرب إلا بالتي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhakkur is repeated remembering; tadhakkarūn is contracted from tatadhakkarūn by assimilation of neighboring consonants.
rows.anchor: وتذكر مطاوع ذكر (¬4) تقول: ذكرته فتذكر

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read tadhakkarūn with a light dhāl, deleting a consonant rather than assimilating it; the author says deletion could be preferable as lighter while meaning remains clear.
rows.anchor: والكسائي (تذكرون (¬2)) خفيفة الذال، خفف بالحذف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: With fatḥa, anna is governed by atlu; alternatively it may be genitive after the command “that is what He enjoined,” as a coordinated item.
rows.anchor: تفتح (أن) من وقوع (أتل)

rows.speaker: أبو علي عن سيبويه
rows.claim: The fatḥa can be governed by “follow it”: because this is My straight path, follow it, paralleling 23:52 and 72:18.
rows.anchor: والتقدير: ولأن {هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه}

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads anna with an open, light hamza; it carries an implicit pronoun of the matter, like al-Aʿshā’s poetic example meaning “he is doomed.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر (¬3): (وأن هذا) مفتوحة مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, in begins a new sentence and the fāʾ coordinates it; on the first analysis the fāʾ is extra, and the case of mustaqīman was explained at 6:126.
rows.anchor: ومن كسر (إن) استأنف بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The straight path is the religion of the ḥanīf, the most upright and best of religions.
rows.anchor: يريد: ديني دين الحنيفية أقوم الأديان وأحسنها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The commands and prohibitions just given are the straight path that people must follow.
rows.anchor: من أمره ونهيه {صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The forbidden side paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and idol worship.
rows.anchor: اليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية وعبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The image is of a traveler leaving the main road for branching paths.
rows.anchor: مثل الذي يسلك الطريق فيأخذ بنيات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The side paths are innovations and doubtful matters.
rows.anchor: يعني: البدع والشبهات

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The paths are misguidance, including forbidding livestock and crops to oneself.
rows.anchor: يعني: طريق الضلالة فيما حرموا على

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ مجاهد
rows.claim: The paths make people stray from God’s religion; Mujāhid glosses the result as deviation and opposition, and says the command is in the Book to guard against those paths.
rows.anchor: فتضل (¬2) بكم عن دينه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Laʿallakum tattaqūn means “so that you may fear.”
rows.anchor: لعلكم تتقون}: (كي تخافوا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: These rulings are decisive, abrogated by nothing in any scripture, forbidden to humanity; those who act on them enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات محكمات، لم ينسخهن شيء في جميع الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb of cutting is intensive because the verse refers to plural hands.
rows.anchor: استعمل لفظ التقطيع هاهنا لمكان الأيدي وهي جمع

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
rows.claim: Min khilāf means cutting opposite-side limbs, such as the right hand and left leg.
rows.anchor: يقطع من كل شق طرف كاليد اليمنى مع الرجل اليسرى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Pharaoh was the first to carry out this form of amputation.
rows.anchor: وفرعون أول من فعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqima means to intensely dislike something, with the phrase discussed at 5:59.
rows.anchor: يقال: نقمت أنقم إذا بالغت في كراهية الشيء

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The magicians say they have committed no offense or harm against Pharaoh that merits punishment, except believing in the signs.
rows.anchor: ما لنا عندك من ذنب ولا ركبنا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Pharaoh reproaches them only for believing Moses’ signs, the staff and hand, came from God, since no one else could produce them.
rows.anchor: وما تطعن علينا (¬2) {إلا أن آمنا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ifrāgh literally means pouring out a vessel’s whole contents; patience is pictured as poured over and surrounding them.
rows.anchor: وأصله من إفراغ الإناء؛ وهو صب ما فيه أجمع حتى يخلو الإناء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They ask for patience during crucifixion and amputation so they will not revert to disbelief.
rows.anchor: اصبب علينا الصبر عند الصلب والقطع حتى لا نرجع كفارا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: They ask God to send down patience that surrounds them, matching the encompassing image of pouring.
rows.anchor: أنزل علينا صبرا يشتمل علينا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They ask to die with sincere devotion in worship.
rows.anchor: مخلصين بالعبادة

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: They ask to die adhering to Moses’ religion.
rows.anchor: على دين موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address “you made a pact” is to the Prophet’s Companions, though the Prophet contracted it; they share the address because they approved his action and thus were as if contracting it themselves.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في {عاهدتم} لأصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج؛ الفراء
rows.claim: Barāʾa may be a predicate, “these verses are a disavowal from God,” or the subject whose predicate is “to those you covenanted”; al-Farrāʾ prefers the first, like saying “handsome, by God” while looking at a man.
rows.anchor: واختار الفراء الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: الفراء؛ الزجاج؛ المفسرون؛ الأزهري
rows.claim: Adhān is coordinated with barāʾa and means public announcement; al-Azharī derives it from the verbal noun īdhān.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الأذان: الإعلام في قول المفسرين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The phrases “from God” and “to the people” modify the announcement; “to” means “for,” and the notice addresses believers and polytheists alike.
rows.anchor: بالناس: المؤمن والمشرك؛ لأن الكل داخلون في هذا الإعلام

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The time phrase may modify the attribute or predicate “God is free of the polytheists,” but not adhān after adhān has been qualified.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {يوم الحج الأكبر}، قال أبو علي:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة؛ عمر؛ سعيد بن المسيب؛ ابن الزبير؛ عطاء؛ طاووس؛ رواية عن علي؛ المسور بن مخرمة عن النبي
rows.claim: They identify the Greater Pilgrimage Day as ʿArafa; a Prophetic report says the sermon at ʿArafa occurred on that day, and the argument is that most pilgrimage is fulfilled by standing there.
rows.anchor: إنه يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء؛ الشعبي؛ النخعي؛ السدي؛ ابن زيد؛ رواية عن علي؛ المغيرة بن شعبة؛ سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: They identify it as the Sacrifice Day because the rites are performed then, while standing at ʿArafa remains valid until dawn; Greater Hajj includes all rites, unlike the lesser pilgrimage, ʿumra.
rows.anchor: يوم الحج الأكبر يوم النحر

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن جريج؛ سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: They identify the Greater Pilgrimage Day as all the days of Minā; “day” can mean a period, as in the multi-day battles called the Day of Ṣiffīn, Jamal, or Buʿāth.
rows.anchor: يوم الحج الأكبر أيام منى # كلها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: In the conditional, istajāraka is jussive though ahad separates it from in; such separation is tolerated especially with in, which is a conditional particle rather than a noun.
rows.anchor: {استجارك} في موضع جزم وإن فرق بين الجازم والمجزوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The seeker of protection is a polytheist who had no treaty.
rows.anchor: ممن لم يكن له عهد

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: He is one of the polytheists whom the Prophet had been ordered to fight.
rows.anchor: من هؤلاء الذين أمرتك بقتالهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A man asked ʿAlī whether a polytheist arriving after the truce to hear God’s word or meet a need would be killed; ʿAlī cited this verse and said no.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل من المشركين إلى علي بن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The request is for protection from killing while the person hears God’s word.
rows.anchor: إن طلب منك أحد منهم أن تجيره من القتل إلى أن يسمع كلام الله

rows.speaker: السدي؛ مقاتل
rows.claim: “God’s word” means the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: “God’s word” includes promises of reward and punishment and the religious obligations of prayer, alms, fasting, pilgrimage, and other duties.
rows.anchor: لأوليائه من الثواب ولأعدائه من العقاب وما افترض في دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bring the person to a place where he is safe; the explanation assumes he has not converted, while a convert becomes a brother in religion.
rows.anchor: يريد: الموضع الذي يأمن فيه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: If the recitation does not persuade the seeker, escort him to safety.
rows.anchor: يقول: إن لم يوافقه ما تتلو

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: They need protection and instruction because they are ignorant of God’s religion, unity, and obligations, and may recognize Islam when taught.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يعرفوا ويجاروا؛ لجهلهم بالعلم فربما يتبينون به الإسلام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Give refuge until the seeker hears God’s word, establish the proof and explain the religion; if he converts he enters Islam’s protection, and if not, return him safely without harassment.
rows.anchor: فإن أسلم فقد دخل في عز الإسلام وإن أبى فأبلغه مأمنه ولا تعرض له

rows.speaker: أهل العلم
rows.claim: A belligerent normally enters Muslim territory with his wealth as war booty unless seeking protection for instruction or trade; a child’s or insane person’s pledge is an ambiguous safe-conduct, while messengers and visitors retrieving protected property also receive safe passage home with person and property protected.
rows.anchor: الكافر الحربي إذا دخل دار الإسلام كان مغنوما مع ماله إلا أن يدخل مستجيرا لغرض شرعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ المفسرون
rows.claim: The one who provides from sky and earth sends rain and brings out plants.
rows.anchor: القطر من السماء ويخرج النبات من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Owning hearing and sight means creating them for people.
rows.anchor: يريد من جعل لكم السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing the living from the dead includes believer from disbeliever, plant from earth, human from sperm, bird from egg, stalk from grain, and palm from seed, with the reverse process likewise.
rows.anchor: أي المؤمن من الكافر، والنبات من الأرض، والإنسان من النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs the affairs of this world and the next; the audience admits He does these things, so they are challenged to fear Him and abandon partners.
rows.anchor: أمر الدنيا والآخرة، {فسيقولون الله}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: After the audience admits that only God can do the things just named, they are told that this is their true Lord.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر عليه إلا الله تعالى: وأقروا به قيل لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The one who does all these things is the truth; the supposed partners possess none of them.
rows.anchor: الذي هذا كله فعله هو الحق ليس هؤلاء الذين جعلتم معه شركاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the truth, the remaining way is their misguidance and the gods they adopted besides God.
rows.anchor: يريد الذي أنتم فيه وما

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: After worshipping God, the only alternative is error: worshipping Satan.
rows.anchor: عبادة الله إلا الضلال، يعني عبادة الشيطان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The closing question asks how reason can turn them to worship beings that neither provide nor give life or death.
rows.anchor: كيف تصرف عقولكم إلى عبادة مالا يرزق ولا يحيى ولا يميت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Losing themselves means ending in Hell; this is the greatest loss because the self has no replacement.
rows.anchor: أي صاروا إلى النار، وخسران النفس أعظم الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabrications fail and bring no benefit in the Afterlife.
rows.anchor: بطل افتراؤهم في الدنيا فلم ينفعهم في الآخرة شيئا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The idols they hoped would benefit them have disappeared.
rows.anchor: ذهبت عنهم الأوثان التي كانوا يؤملون بها الانتفاع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Lā jarama means surely, certainly.
rows.anchor: يقول: حقا إنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Lā jarama originally meant “no escape” or “inevitably,” later becoming an emphatic “truly” and sometimes functioning like an oath.
rows.anchor: كلمة كانت في الأصل بمنزلة

rows.speaker: الزجاج؛ الأزهري؛ ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says lā denies the assumed benefit and jarama means earned: their deed earned loss; al-Azharī calls this one of the best explanations, and Ibn al-Anbārī analyzes jarama as a past verb with an implicit subject referring to disbelief.
rows.anchor: معنى لا جرم: (لا) نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another explanation treats lā as extra, so their deed earned them regret.
rows.anchor: (لا) صلة في {لا جرم} والمعنى: كسب لهم عملهم الندامة

rows.speaker: الأخفش؛ سيبويه
rows.claim: They take lā as a rejection of the disbelievers’ claim and jarama as “deserved/was certain”; the cited poem uses jaramat to mean that a spear thrust made Ghatafān angry.
rows.anchor: جرم معناه أحق صحيح

rows.speaker: الفراء؛ أبو العباس
rows.claim: They reject that interpretation, reading Ghatafān as accusative: the wound caused the tribe to become angry.
rows.anchor: جرمت فزاره بالنصب، والمعنى جرمتهم الطعنة أن يغضبوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers slaughtered a lamb, smeared its blood on Joseph’s shirt, and had left him naked in the well.
rows.anchor: ذبحوا سخلة وجلوا دمها على قميص يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They came in the evening to use the darkness to excuse themselves and make their deception more persuasive; their weeping was staged to seem innocent of the alleged wolf attack.
rows.anchor: ليكونوا أجرا في الظلمة على الاعتذار وترويج

rows.speaker: مجالد عن الشعبي
rows.claim: Shurayḥ answered a woman who wept in court by recalling that Joseph’s brothers had also come to their father weeping at night.
rows.anchor: قد جاء إخوة يوسف أباهم عشاء يبكون

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين؛ الزجاج؛ ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Nastabiqu means competing in archery, supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh as nantaṣilu and the Prophetic rule that prizes are only for camels, arrows, or horses; archers compare whose arrow travels farther.
rows.anchor: نتنصل في الرمي، وهذا اختيار الزجاج

rows.speaker: السدي؛ مقاتل
rows.claim: They interpret it as running hard to see who is faster; though this seems childish for adult men, training their running prepared them for war and defending livestock from enemies or wolves.
rows.anchor: نستبق: نشتد ونعدو لنتبين أينا أسرع عدوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers left Joseph with their clothes and belongings.
rows.anchor: يريد ثيابهم

rows.speaker: عامة المفسرين؛ أصحاب المعاني
rows.claim: Muʾmin means believing or accepting their account; the author refers to the discussion at the opening of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: مصدق لنا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق؛ أبو العباس
rows.claim: “Even if truthful” does not accuse the prophet Jacob of disbelieving known truth; the brothers mean his suspicion and intense love of Joseph would make him distrust them regardless.
rows.anchor: ليسوا يريدون أن يعقوب لا يصدق من يعلم أنه صادق

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: They may mean they believe themselves truthful but Jacob will not be persuaded without signs; even objective truth does not establish their credibility to him.
rows.anchor: نحن صادقون عند أنفسنا، وأنت غير مصدق لنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ مجاهد؛ عامة المفسرين
rows.claim: The blood on Joseph’s shirt was from a slaughtered lamb; other reports suggest a kid goat or camel calf.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك دم سخلة

rows.speaker: الفراء؛ أبو العباس؛ الزجاج؛ ابن الأنباري؛ الأخفش
rows.claim: Bi-damin kadhib means blood falsely claimed to be Joseph’s; the verbal noun kadhib describes the object for emphasis, as in “unprofitable trade” and other source-noun adjectives.
rows.anchor: أي مكذوب فيه، إلا أنه وصف بالمصدر على تقدير: ذي كذب

rows.speaker: الحسن؛ سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Jacob calls the story a lie: a wolf would not have eaten his son without tearing the shirt.
rows.anchor: قال: كذبتم، ما عهدي

rows.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another account Jacob says the wolf was unusually gentle; when the brothers blame robbers, he asks why they left the shirt, which they needed more than the killing.
rows.anchor: لقد كان هذا الذئب رفيقا حين أكل ابني ولم يخرق قميصه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ عامة المفسرين
rows.claim: Sawwalat means their selves adorned or made the deed seem attractive to them.
rows.anchor: زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني؛ الأزهري
rows.claim: Taswīl is forming a hoped-for wish in the soul; al-Azharī relates it to a desired ambition that beautifies falsehood and worldly aims, with hamza softened because frequent use made it burdensome.
rows.anchor: التسويل تقدير معنى في النفس على الطمع في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal rejects the brothers’ wolf account and replaces it with the charge that their own selves devised another matter.
rows.anchor: وقوله {بل} رد لقولهم: أكله الذئب

rows.speaker: مجاهد؛ المفسرون
rows.claim: Beautiful patience means enduring without despair or complaint; a Prophetic report defines it as patience without complaint, with no grading stated.
rows.anchor: هو صبر لا شكوى فيه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Beautiful patience shows no visible change, such as a frown or withdrawal from one’s former openness.
rows.anchor: أن يصبر حتى لا يظهر فيه تغير بعبوس وجه

rows.speaker: الخليل؛ قطرب؛ الفراء؛ أبو عبيد؛ الزجاج؛ ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: They supply different implied predicates for the nominative ṣabrun: what I believe, my patience, it is, let it be mine, my affair, or equivalent meanings.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل (¬6): معناه: فالذي أعتقده صبر جميل

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق؛ أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Outside Qurʾānic wording, ṣabran jamīlan is possible; raising is preferable when patience is described, while accusative suits an indefinite standalone noun, with poetry illustrating the accusative.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن: فصبرا جميلا

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Appealing to God for help expresses the piety that calls for beautiful patience and reliance on God amid terrible events.
rows.anchor: هذا بيان عما يوجبه التقى من الصبر الجميل عند المصيبة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The object of “He gave you” is omitted: He gave you something from everything requested, like other verses that omit “something.”
rows.anchor: المفعول محذوف تقديره من كل مسؤول شيئا أو مسؤولا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: On Abū al-Ḥasan’s grammatical analysis, the prepositional phrase is accusative and min is extra even in an affirmative clause.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الجار والمجرور في موضع

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: God gives what people asked for and what they never requested, such as sun and moon; mentioning requests can stand for unasked gifts, as in the clothing that protects from heat.
rows.anchor: وما لم تسألوه؛ لأنا لم نسأله شمسا ولا قمرا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري؛ الكسائي
rows.claim: Another reading is that God gave whatever people wish, desire, or prefer; al-Kisāʾī notes that asking language can mean getting one’s wish, not literal questioning.
rows.anchor: وآتاكم من كل ما تتمنون تشتهون وتؤثرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmat is a verbal noun standing for inʿām, so it remains singular as an infinitive would.
rows.anchor: النعمة هاهنا اسم أقيم مقام المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā tuḥṣūhā means you cannot count all God’s abundant favors, as 72:28 says He encompasses the number of all things.
rows.anchor: لا يأتوا على جميعها بالعد لكثرتها

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Lā tuḥṣūhā can mean that people cannot preserve or remember the favors.
rows.anchor: لا تحفظوها

rows.speaker: أبو العالية؛ الفراء؛ غيره
rows.claim: A further gloss is inability to endure or perform the favors; these two readings also occur at 73:20, where al-Farrāʾ interprets it as keeping night-vigil times and others as being unable to bear it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا تطيقون عدها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: This rebukes ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, al-Aqraʿ, and leaders proud of wealth and children: these adorn worldly life but do not benefit in the Hereafter; the enduring good deeds contrast with what Salman and Suhayb do.
rows.anchor: هذا رد على عيينة بن حصين، والأقرع والرؤساء الذين كانوا يفتخرون بالمال والغنى والأبناء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير؛ مسروق؛ إبراهيم؛ محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: One interpretation of the enduring good deeds is the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: هي الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء؛ مجاهد؛ عكرمة؛ الضحاك
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the glorifications: subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.
rows.anchor: يريد سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: أنس؛ أبو هريرة؛ الخدري؛ عثمان؛ ابن عمر؛ سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: A Prophetic report names those remembrances the enduring good deeds; another group adds lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh.
rows.anchor: أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- سمى هذه الأذكار الباقيات الصالحات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية العوفي
rows.claim: The phrase can mean good speech, which is also a form of remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: هي الكلام الطيب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي؛ قتادة؛ الزجاج
rows.claim: It can mean righteous deeds and all good actions done for God; al-Zajjāj chooses every righteous deed whose reward remains.
rows.anchor: هي كل عمل صالح يبقى ثوابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الفراء
rows.claim: The enduring deeds are better in reward and hope than wealth and children; Arabic uses “better” even where the comparison offers nothing good, and hope in good work surpasses hope in evil work.
rows.anchor: يريد أفضل ثوابا وأفضل أملا من المال والبنين

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Better hope means better than what people hope to obtain from wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: ({وخير أملا} مما يؤملون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most lost are those who reject God’s signs, the evidence of His oneness and power, and the meeting of resurrection, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: جحدوا دلائل توحيده وقدرته {ولقائه} وكفروا بالبعث، والثواب، والعقاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Their deeds came to nothing: their striving was nullified.
rows.anchor: بطل اجتهادهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون عن أبي هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a huge, tall, gluttonous man will weigh less than a mosquito’s wing, then cites this verse; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ليؤتين يوم القيامة بالعظيم، الطويل، الشروب، الأكلول فلا يزن عند الله جناح بعوضة

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة؛ عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: They report a man weighed against a grain and then a mosquito’s wing without weighing even that much, and recite the verse.
rows.anchor: يؤتى برجل يوم القيامة فيوزن بحبة فلا يزنها

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They have no weight because only someone with righteous deeds and monotheistic faith is weighed.
rows.anchor: إنما يوزن من له عمل صالح، وكان على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author؛ أبو العباس عن ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: The reports seem to weigh the men themselves, but the author rejects that reading: deeds are weighed, and “has no weight” idiomatically means having no worth or standing with God; even the enormous glutton in the hadith lacks value without monotheism.
rows.anchor: والصحيح في هذا ما قاله أهل المعاني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the unbelievers’ scales are light in good deeds because they lack the monotheism that makes the scales heavy.
rows.anchor: خفة موازينهم من الحسنات

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The apparent weighing of unbelievers can be retained as a humiliation, showing all creatures that they weigh less than an atom or mosquito’s wing.
rows.anchor: يأمر بوزن أهل الكفر تحقيرا لهم، وتصغيرا لأمرهم
